name: North Korea
summary: Founded in 1948 in the Soviet-occupied north; ruled by the Kim family; one of the most closed states in the world, with nuclear weapons.

location.source: Britannica: North Korea facts (checked 9 Nov 2026); corrected from 120,500 km²

terrain.value: About 80 percent mountains and hills, with small coastal plains in the west and east.

climate.value: Continental, with cold, dry winters and hot, rainy summers.

resources.value: Coal, iron ore and other minerals, and hydropower.

population.source: Britannica: North Korea facts, 2026 estimate (checked 9 Nov 2026); corrected from about 26 million (2024)

urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: Pyongyang (checked 9 Nov 2026)

disease.value: Hunger and weak health care are reported, especially after the famine of the 1990s.

migration.value: Some people have fled through China to South Korea; defectors number in the tens of thousands.

economicBase.value: State-run heavy industry, mining, farming and weapons production under central planning.

tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Korea Times, Statistics Korea data: about 98% of trade with China (checked 9 Nov 2026)

wealth.value: Very poor, with a much smaller economy than South Korea.

moneyAndTax.value: The North Korean won; the state owns most property and sets prices.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: Korean Workers’ Party (checked 9 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Kim Il Sung. Kim Jong Il. Later and present leaders are not named here.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: history of North Korea; Britannica: Kim Jong Un (checked 9 Nov 2026)

succession.source: Britannica: Kim Jong Il (succeeded Kim Il Sung, 1994); Kim Jong Un (2011) (checked 9 Nov 2026)

institutions.value: The Workers’ Party of Korea, a one-party system, with the Supreme People’s Assembly as a formal parliament.

stability.value: A one-party state kept stable by strict control and a large security apparatus.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; RFE/RL: first nuclear test, 9 Oct 2006 (checked 9 Nov 2026)

majorWars.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: Korean War (25 Jun 1950 – 27 Jul 1953) (checked 9 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: division of Korea (1945–48) (checked 9 Nov 2026)

alliancesRivals.value: China is the main trading partner and ally; Russia has close links; South Korea and the United States are the main rivals.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: State schooling is universal; the state focuses on missiles, nuclear weapons and computer technology.

openness.value: One of the most closed countries in the world: travel, media and the internet are tightly restricted.

communicationTransport.value: Few private cars; railways and buses carry most people, and roads outside the capital are limited.

religion.value: Officially atheist; the state promotes the “Juche” ideology and veneration of the ruling family.

languageWriting.value: Korean, written in Hangul; Chinese characters are no longer used in daily writing.

artsArchitecture.value: Monumental statues and buildings, mass games, and the Pyongyang skyline.

socialStructure.value: The “songbun” system ranked people by perceived loyalty to the state.

sharedIdentity.value: Official ideology stresses Juche and loyalty to the ruling Kim family.

neighbours.value: China, Russia (a short border) and South Korea (across the Demilitarised Zone).

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: Juche (checked 9 Nov 2026)

colonisation.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: Korea under Japanese rule (checked 9 Nov 2026)

riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: North Korea; Britannica: history of North Korea (checked 9 Nov 2026)

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: North Korea continues as a state.

overallCertainty.value: Many figures are estimates; the state releases little data.
